name: What We Got Wrong Last Week
why_it_works: Admitting a mistake is rare in ads, so it stops the scroll. Owning a small, real error and showing the exact fix proves the business pays attention, which builds more trust than any claim of perfection.

hook.pattern: Open with a plain admission of a specific recent mistake.
examples: We messed up last week. This is what happened.
A customer caught our mistake. They were right.
Our worst {{mistake_area}} moment this month, and the fix.

variables.name: cause
variables.description: The real behind-the-scenes cause, written as a sentence starting with a capital

variables.name: fix
variables.description: What changed, written as a sentence starting with a capital
variables.example: A backup screen and a five-minute ticket check

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Make-good or next step, a full sentence starting with a capital, 6 words or fewer

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. Consult a licensed provider.

visual.prompt: Real phone footage of the {{brand}} owner speaking straight to camera in their own words after close, honest flat light, chest-up, vertical 9:16
Candid shot of the {{brand}} workspace during a busy rush, work piling up, motion blur, no faces, practical light, vertical 9:16
Close-up of the piece of equipment or step behind {{cause}}, flat work light, slightly gritty, vertical 9:16
Close-up of hands using the new fix at {{brand}}, {{fix}}, no faces, steady handheld shot, clean bright light, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: The trust comes from the specific cause and the specific fix, not the apology. Keep the mistake small and real, name it in under ten words, and spend more seconds on the fix than on the error.

do_not: Blame a staff member or a customer by name
Admit to anything with legal or safety implications without advice first
compliance: Med spa: never discuss a patient's treatment or complication publicly, and share nothing without written consent (HIPAA); keep mistakes to operations (booking, wait times); no before/after or results claims, results vary
Financial advisor: do not discuss any client's account or losses; no income or return promises; include required firm disclosures
Restaurants: any food-safety issue goes to your health department process first, not to social media
Coaches: no income or results promises; any result shown is labelled as not typical
